citation: Preschool Curriculum Evaluation Research Consortium. (2008). Effects of Preschool Curriculum Programs on School Readiness: Report from the Preschool Curriculum Evaluation Research Initiative (NCER 2008-2009). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Research, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education. U.S. Government Printing Office. ERIC No. ED502153.
design: Cluster-randomized RCT (efficacy). 12 research teams independently evaluated 14 preschool curricula (Creative Curriculum was evaluated twice -> 15 curriculum-vs-control arms). Within each team/site, preschools/classrooms (or Pre-K programs) were randomly assigned to an intervention curriculum vs a control (business-as-usual / locally-developed) curriculum; children (~2,911 total across 315 classrooms / 208 preschools) were followed from pre-K through kindergarten. Each curriculum was implemented with teacher training/support (TPD for curricula). Assignment unit = classroom or Pre-K program (registry labels 'School'). Subjects: early reading/literacy, phonological awareness, language, early mathematics (+behavior, excluded). Grade = Pre-K. Outcomes at end of pre-K (spring pre-K = immediate post) and end of kindergarten (follow-up).
problems:
MULTI-CURRICULUM REPORT CODED AS ONE REGISTRY ROW (row_id 89). This single IES report (NCER 2008-2009) evaluates 14 distinct preschool curricula (Creative Curriculum twice -> 15 curriculum-vs-control arms) at 12 sites, each a separate cluster-RCT against its own local business-as-usual/teacher-developed control. I extracted ALL 135 student-ACHIEVEMENT contrasts (9 child academic measures x 15 arms): reading (TERA, WJ Letter-Word ID, WJ Spelling) and phonological awareness (Pre-CTOPPP) -> Reading; language (PPVT, TOLD Grammatic Understanding) -> Other; math (WJ Applied Problems, CMA-A Mathematics Composite, Shape Composition) -> STEM. I SKIPPED all behavior outcomes (SSRS Social Skills, SSRS Problem Behavior, PLBS/LBS) as non-academic, and all classroom-level outcomes (ECERS-R, Arnett, TBRS) as teacher/classroom not student achievement. The original meta-analysis (Visscher et al. 2025) likely used only a subset (e.g., one Reading composite per curriculum, or only DLM-with-Open-Court / Pre-K-Math which were the curricula with significant achievement impacts); the central team must decide which arm(s)/measure(s) map to row 89. 

EFFECT-SIZE METHOD: the point estimate g uses the report's published Table E effect size d (spring pre-K, end-of-treatment) where d = (covariate-adjusted M_T - M_C)/sigma_pooled, sigma_pooled = a SITE-SPECIFIC model-based pooled population SD (Appendix B eqs.10-16; a null HLM with classroom random effect, weighted across groups and the first two time points). g = J*d, J=1-3/(4*df-1), df=n_t+n_c-2. Because each effect size uses its own site-specific normalizer (NOT the global SDs in Tables B-6/B-9), I derived g_se per cell from the Appendix-D spring-pre-K covariate-adjusted mean difference (impact_estimate, raw units) and its SE (impact_se, raw units): implied site SD = mean_diff / d_TableE, then SE_in_d = SE_meandiff / SD, g_se = J*SE_in_d. This recovers the exact normalizer the report used for each cell and is internally consistent (verified: DLM TERA d=.68, mean_diff=5.42 -> SD=7.97, g_se=.175). 

CLUSTER & PRETEST: the Table-E d and the Appendix-D mean diff/SE come from a hierarchical linear (mixed) model with a random classroom intercept (children nested in classrooms; inferences generalized to the population), so they ACCOUNT FOR CLUSTERING -> cluster_adjusted=true; and the child models include the fall pre-K baseline score as a covariate (ANCOVA / repeated-measures-spline) -> pretest_adjusted=true. n_clusters per arm = treatment + control classrooms (or Pre-K programs) from Table B-1. NO design-effect/outcome ICC is reported anywhere; icc left null (NOT guessed). 

MODEL NUANCE: most measures (reading, language, math) were modeled with a repeated-measures linear SPLINE over 3 time points; the 'spring pre-K' effect size is the model-estimated group mean difference at the spring pre-K node. Phonological awareness (Pre-CTOPPP) used a SIMPLE repeated-measures model over 2 time points (fall + spring pre-K). 

TABLE TRANSCRIPTION ARTIFACTS / FALLBACKS (10 cells): for 10 contrasts the Table-E d and the Appendix-D spring-pre-K mean diff have inconsistent sign or a zero, so the clean SE derivation was impossible and I used a STUDENT-LEVEL design-based fallback variance (Var(d)=(n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c)+d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c)), g_var=J^2*Var(d)); these are NOT cluster-adjusted (flagged in each g_method). Affected: all Pre-CTOPPP cells where Table-E d (a small positive) does not match the Appendix-D spring-pre-K mean diff (Pre-CTOPPP's simple-RM effect-size convention differs from the spring-pre-K mean-difference reported in App D) -- Creative Curriculum(V), Curiosity Corner, Project Approach, Project Construct; near-zero math cells where d rounds to a different sign than a ~0.00 mean diff (Curiosity Corner CMA, ELLM CMA); Pre-K Mathematics WJ Letter-Word ID (Table E d=.42 vs App D mean diff=-0.31 -- a clear sign/magnitude mismatch in the report's own tables, flagged); Project Approach WJ Spelling (Table E prints '27' with no decimal -- a typographic artifact; used App D mean diff=6.35/SE=8.80 to derive, d set to 0 placeholder so this cell is design-based fallback, see note); Project Construct TERA (Table E .00 vs App D -0.01). 

APPENDIX-D POSSIBLE OVERLAP: Table D-8a (ELLM) math rows are numerically identical to Table D-5a (Curiosity Corner) math rows in the PDF, which may be a report transcription overlap; ELLM math values were used as printed in D-8a and flagged. 

RAW MEANS/SDs left null: the report does not publish per-group adjusted posttest means with the standardizing SD inline; it publishes the d (Table E), the covariate-adjusted mean DIFFERENCE + SE (App D), and pooled SDs (App B). I recorded impact_estimate/impact_se = the raw-unit mean diff/SE; g/g_se are standardized as described. TIMEPOINT = immediate post (spring pre-K, end of the one-year curriculum). Kindergarten (Table F) is a later follow-up wave and was NOT extracted.
